profiles.meeting_scenario: The meeting is a design review for the proposed production-oriented version of SecureReviewer, an internal LLM-based assistant that will generate security-focused code review comments on pull requests. The team has already completed a research prototype showing improved secure code review performance through secure-aware fine-tuning, RAG over security documentation, and the SecureBLEU metric. In this review, they are evaluating whether the current design is sufficient for an engineering pilot inside the company's GitHub Enterprise workflow. The agenda is to review the proposed architecture for retrieval grounding, the expected form of generated fix suggestions, the evaluation and approval bar for a pilot, and the rollout plan for the initial Java service repositories. The expected outcome is a decision on whether to approve the design as pilot-ready with minor edits, or to request modifications before implementation begins.

members.name: Nina Patel
members.expertise: LLM fine-tuning, code intelligence systems, retrieval-augmented generation, offline evaluation of developer tools
members.background: Nina previously built an internal general-purpose PR comment assistant and is now adapting that platform for security-focused review. She has strong experience with model behavior, benchmark design, and integrating ML tooling into developer workflows.
members.private_state: Nina wants the design approved quickly so she can reuse the existing PR assistant infrastructure and hit the quarter's pilot milestone. She is trying to preserve as much of the research prototype as possible, especially the existing retrieval pipeline and offline evaluation package, because major changes would delay engineering handoff.
hidden_assumptions: The 'security knowledge base' naturally includes all internal security-related documents already accessible to employees, including wiki pages and past incident write-ups, not just formally versioned standards.
A 'fix suggestion' is successful if it points the developer toward the right mitigation pattern or safer API, even if it does not provide an exact patch-level edit.
A design can be considered 'pilot-ready' once offline evaluation is strong and a limited shadow review with sampled human feedback looks promising.
When people mention the 'six pilot repos,' they usually mean the mirrored evaluation copies with replayed PR history, since those are what the ML team has been using for validation.

members.name: Marcus Lee
members.expertise: Secure SDLC, code review policy, vulnerability triage, enterprise rollout of security tooling
members.background: Marcus leads application security guidance for product teams and has overseen multiple secure coding tool rollouts, including SAST and dependency scanning integrations. He is responsible for ensuring that developer-facing security guidance is accurate, policy-compliant, and operationally safe.
members.private_state: Marcus wants SecureReviewer to be useful, but only if it behaves like an extension of approved AppSec guidance rather than a research demo. He is particularly worried about the tool surfacing advice that conflicts with official standards or creating noisy comments on live repositories that teams will quickly learn to ignore.
hidden_assumptions: The 'security knowledge base' means only curated, approved, versioned sources intended to provide normative developer guidance, such as the secure coding standard, ASVS mappings, and vetted playbooks.
A 'fix suggestion' should be concrete enough that a developer could directly translate it into a code change or patch with minimal extra interpretation.
Something is only 'pilot-ready' after it has survived a live silent-mode trial with operational guardrails, because offline gains do not establish deployment safety.

References to the 'six pilot repos' point to the actual volunteer teams' active repositories in GitHub Enterprise, since a pilot by definition concerns real workflows rather than mirrored test environments.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the security knowledge base
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss grounding SecureReviewer with 'the security knowledge base.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina means a broad internal corpus: CWE entries, OWASP material, the internal secure coding wiki, incident postmortems, and past advisory pages that are searchable and useful for retrieval.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means a narrow approved corpus: versioned secure coding standards, vetted remediation playbooks, and officially sanctioned guidance intended for developer-facing recommendations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In the organization, people casually use 'security knowledge base' as a catch-all phrase, so the boundary between searchable security documents and policy-approved guidance is rarely restated unless there is a compliance incident.

misalignment_points.topic: What a fix suggestion should look like
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the model should provide 'fix suggestions' instead of just flagging issues.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina means the comment should identify the vulnerability and recommend the right mitigation direction, such as using parameterized queries or validating redirects with an allowlist.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the comment should be actionable at near-patch level, such as pointing to the concrete safe helper, expected validation call, or code pattern the team should replace.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see 'fix suggestion' as obviously better than issue-only comments, so the conversation stays at the level of shared intent and never drills into how specific or code-adjacent the suggestion must be.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about getting the design 'ready for pilot' this quarter.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina means the design is ready once offline metrics on held-out repos are solid, red-team checks look acceptable, and a small reviewer sample rates the generated comments as useful in shadow review.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the design is ready only after a live silent-mode run on real repositories demonstrates safe operational behavior, including stable false-positive patterns and a suppression/escalation path.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because 'pilot' is already an intermediate milestone, each assumes the other is using the standard gate from their own function: research-to-engineering handoff for Nina, deployment safety gate for Marcus.

misalignment_points.topic: Which six pilot repos are being discussed
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the six Java pilot repos' as the target set.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina is thinking of the mirrored repositories in the evaluation environment, which replay recent PR history and are safe for offline and shadow experiments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus is thinking of the six volunteer product teams' active repositories where the silent-mode pilot would ultimately run.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The mirrored repos preserve the same names and team labels as the live repositories, so references to them sound identical in conversation unless someone explicitly distinguishes mirror versus production org.
